claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 conventionally requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventional high-temperature preparation of ZrB2 produces higher porosity and structural defects because of prolonged high-temperature exposure.
SPS at 1800–2000 °C can consolidate a single-phase ZrB2 ceramic.
ZrB2 processed by SPS at 1800–2000 °C will be denser and less porous than ZrB2 conventionally sintered above 2300 °C.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will retain greater structural integrity during long-term liquid plating bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
A pressure around 30 MPa and a dwell time of 5–10 minutes are suitable SPS conditions for the proposed ZrB2 preparation.
Rapid heating and short SPS dwell times minimize grain growth.
The fast SPS process increases densification and reduces porosity.
Increased densification and reduced porosity produce fewer structural defects and improve grain-boundary integrity.
Rapid heating and applied electrical current in SPS enhance mass transport and densification kinetics.
Enhanced SPS densification kinetics enable effective ceramic consolidation at temperatures below those required by conventional processing.
SPS prevents excessive grain growth and reduces hole formation in ZrB2.
Reducing holes preserves ZrB2 structural integrity during prolonged contact with a liquid plating bath.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have higher hardness and fracture toughness than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have greater durability during long-duration liquid plating exposure.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 tends to have significant porosity and declining integrity in corrosive or liquid plating environments.
Optimization of SPS pressure, duration, and temperature may be required to obtain a consistently dense single phase.
